output.name: Sokul — The Stooping Gull
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went off like a sail torn from its mast, and Tavo laughed until the cliffs rang. A gull named Sokul was working the north ledges that morning with a cod in its beak. It saw the sky leaving and went after it, higher than any gull had flown. Halun, the Gull Who Waited, watches from the north-west and has never come down, so it saw what came next and kept quiet. Tavo took Sokul by one wingtip and bent it back, and Sokul had to stoop to come home, and it came home with the fish still in its beak. Hesk counted the wing. Hasket, the drop spindle that slipped from her fingers, still turns in the north-east and watches the bird too. Ennu says the bend is why the gulls ride the wind so close to the cliffs, always testing it. The Gulls say Sokul is still aloft, and that when its bent wing points at the house, someone will fly back. Mend your own tears with sinew. Watch the gull's wing before you fly.
output.finding: Find Halun, the Gull Who Waited, and sight a fist and a half (about 14°) south-east of it, where Sokul hangs with its bent wing and its cod.
